summary:
Ebeye is the most populous island of Kwajalein Atoll and the Marshall Islands’ second most populous island. About 8,416 people lived on its 80 acres in 2021, making it one of the world’s most densely populated small islands. A causeway completed in 1992 links it to several islands to the north; the nearby military base on Kwajalein provides employment and logistical support.

Many residents were relocated to Ebeye in the 1950s and 1960s as the United States used other atoll islands for military activities and missile testing. Some residents are refugees or descendants of people displaced by the 1954 Castle Bravo nuclear test.

Ebeye has schools, health facilities, stores, docks, and the Republic of the Marshall Islands’ Emergency Operations Center, opened in 2024. Water shortages, waste management, and overcrowding remain concerns. More than 33% of residents have diabetes, linked in the article to limited access to fresh food. Planned and ongoing aid projects address water, sewage, and protection from waves that can flood the low-lying island. The local economy depends partly on U.S. aid and military-related activity.
